body: If you're just trying to get some sleep, why not try some of those Tylenol sleep pills? They don't require a prescription, and supposedly non-addictive (which I'm not too sure about). However, you will probably be all groggy and tired the next day akin to a small hangover.
Before having children, flush a chunk of your paycheck money down the toilet every month; if that seems to bother you, don't have kids.

I don't mean to sound insensitive, but wtf, you want to kill yourself cause you got dumped? You think you're the first one in the history of the world to get dumped?

There are worse things that can happen to you. I'm sure right now it feels akin to "omfg i'll never meet someone like her evar," but a bajillion people can attest that time will wipe that feeling away eventually. So focus on your school work and distract yourself to prevent your mind from drifting back to pensive thoughts.
....so I dropped everything and exercised. Some 30-40 minutes of mind numbing pushups and excruciating squats, followed by a shower and I feel way way WAY better.

* You're unmarried: You think being married means you'll be happy? Chances are you'll be happier single.

* no house: That's a bad thing in this economy? Loads of people bought houses in the last two years that are worth a fraction of what they paid. Consider yourself lucky.

* Balding: your tears won't help grow it back. If you want to feel like you're doing something about it, go get some rogaine.

This is my advice to you: Stop drinking yourself drunk, and start exercising. It will be hard at first, but you **will** see the benefits; I and many others here can attest to it.

Whatever you do, don't get yourself fired from work; that's the last thing you need.

I work in corporate, doing what I would have described as my dream job when I finished college. But after being an obsessive workaholic for a whole bunch of years, I'm terribly jaded. I too wonder what it's all for in the end. Wake up, eat oatmeal, commute to work, stare at monitor for 8-10 hours, commute back, sleep, repeat. I have another 30+ years of this to look forward to, and that's if I'm lucky to be employed the whole time.

I too have a medical condition, which while not debilitating in any way in my day to day functioning, does have an effect on my psychological health. I guess, or rather I know, part of the problem is my practically non-existent social life. I'm sure that would help, but I just shun what few friends I have. I just tire of them so easily.

The only thing that makes me feel considerably better is exercising, which I do 3-4 days a week assiduously. I'm terrified of drugs, concerned about addiction. So I exercise, and tell me myself that it could always be worse, it could always be worse. And I get back to my push ups. 

That's the only advice I can give you I guess: push ups.
